FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
New residents face a ninety-day clock to qualify for a Texas license, while service members keep an existing Texas card valid through duty plus ninety days after [A01].
Why it matters: group residency-rules; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F01 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
A learner card costs sixteen dollars total and ends at eighteen, while a practicing adult pays thirty-three dollars total for eight restricted years [A01].
Why it matters: group license-terms; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F02 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A02
A school VOE stays fresh thirty days in session but ninety days across summer [A02].
Why it matters: group school-paperwork; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F03 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A02
Hardship approval turns on proven need and narrow grounds, while graduated Phase One turns on a six-month learner hold that suspensions stretch [A02].
Why it matters: group teen-paths; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F03; confusables sec01-F04 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A03
Phase Two caps young non-family riders at one and separately bans midnight-to-five driving outside work, school, or emergency [A03].
Why it matters: group teen-limits; difficulty low; prereq sec01-F04; confusables sec01-F05 [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A03
PROVISIONAL marks sixteen- to eighteen-year-old license holders, while UNDER twenty-one marks every card issued before twenty-one [A03].
Why it matters: group card-markings; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F06 [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A04
Class A combinations are judged by combined weight with heavy towed weight, while Class B singles are judged by single-vehicle weight with lighter towing caps [A04].
Why it matters: group license-classes; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec01-F07 [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A04
Class C prices split three ways by path, thirty-three dollars total as an adult, sixteen dollars total at sixteen with education, or six dollars total at fifteen with hardship [A04].
Why it matters: group license-terms; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F07; confusables sec01-F08 [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A05
Appending M to a live license costs sixteen dollars total, while renewing M adds twelve dollars total on top of renewal [A05].
Why it matters: group license-terms; difficulty low; prereq sec01-F08; confusables sec01-F09 [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A06
The donor heart on the card front is binding consent for gifts, while the five contribution checkboxes are optional donations [A06].
Why it matters: group card-choices; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F11 [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A07
Exam failure parks an application ninety days, while exam success earns a forty-five-day temporary card [A07].
Why it matters: group exam-admin; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F14 [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A07
Class C, Class M, and Class A and B exams each test different drivers, yet every one passes at seventy percent or better [A07].
Why it matters: group exam-admin; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F14 [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A08
Stepping up a class or shedding restrictions costs ten dollars, appending Class M costs fifteen dollars, and any exam fails past thirty lost points [A08].
Why it matters: group exam-admin; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F14; confusables sec01-F15 [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A09
Unlicensed fines rise from two hundred dollars first to a twenty-five-to-two-hundred-dollar band on a second within a year, then leap to Class A jail for deadly uninsured crashes [A09].
Why it matters: group penalties; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F17 [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A10
Licenses renew every eight years, yet every driver still appears in person at least each sixteen years for vision and biometrics [A10].
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F19 [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A11
Hearing review follows four convictions in twelve months but needs seven in twenty-four [A11].
Why it matters: group suspension-triggers; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F20; confusables sec01-F22 [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A12
Revocation starts at point zero eight for twenty-one-plus drivers but at any detectable alcohol under twenty-one [A12].
Why it matters: group alcohol-limits; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F23 [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A13
Zero Tolerance suspensions climb thirty, sixty, then one hundred eighty days across offenses, with the oldest teens reaching Class B and denied deferral [A13].
Why it matters: group penalties; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F25; confusables sec01-F26 [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0019]
